BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, tessarákonta means forty. In Matthew 4:2, he had fasted forty days and forty nights, and it appears again in Acts 7:30. In the Greek text the word is spelled τεσσεράκοντα.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that forty days and forty years in Scripture are never wasted time; God uses the long stretch to prove and prepare His people.
